battle.name: 南北戰爭
battle.theater: 維吉尼亞戰區與西部戰線
battle.brief: 一八六一年四月，南方十一州退出聯邦，內戰在查爾斯頓港的薩姆特堡打響。卡面雷管步槍把有效射程推到二百碼以上，拿破崙式縱隊在弗雷德里克斯堡與冷港前撞上散兵與塹壕，戰爭因此變成一場比工業、比鐵路、比動員的消耗。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰的兩方是美國聯邦與美利堅聯邦國。聯邦方面由三十四州中的二十三州組成：南卡羅來納等十一州相繼退出聯邦後，林肯於一八六一年三月就任臨時總統，四月十八日下令徵召七萬五千名民兵，北方各州按人口比例提供志願兵，基層編制是兵營，步兵營約五百至一千人，營下設連，每連八十至一百人，二十四連組成約兩千人的旅，旅以上是師。志願兵制動員極快，代價是軍官缺乏經驗，裝備與訓練由各州自理而非聯邦統籌，各州之間水平相差極大。聯邦於一八六三年三月頒布《徵兵法》，以抽籤或繳納代役金取代購買代替役，黑人士兵自一八六二年起獲准入伍，編為美國有色步兵團。海軍方面由戰初約一百三十艘艦艇擴張到一八六五年逾六百艘，並催生鐵甲艦、水雷與單裝魚雷。邦聯方面由十一州組成，一八六一年二月在蒙哥馬利成立政府，四月遷都里奇蒙。其結構弱點在於主權歸州：各州自行決定供兵、鑄幣與徵兵，州長可拒絕執行邦聯命令，軍隊編制與人事由州政府掌握，因而形成十支以上編號互不歸屬的州軍，即使由李維斯或約翰斯頓統率的維吉尼亞軍與田納西軍，兵源補充仍受制於州議會。邦聯沒有聯邦兵工廠體系，槍械靠州級兵工廠與海外採購，軍官晉升因兵員暴增而失序，戰爭後段尤其嚴重。
countriesEn: The two sides were the federal government of the United States and the Confederate States of America. The Union was built from twenty-three of the thirty-four states: after eleven states had seceded, Lincoln took office as provisional president in March 1861, and on 18 April he called for seventy-five thousand militia volunteers, the northern states furnishing men in proportion to population. The base unit was the battalion, five hundred to a thousand men, divided into companies of eighty to a hundred; twenty-four companies made a brigade of about two thousand men, and brigades were stacked into divisions. The volunteer system mobilised with remarkable speed, but it left the army without a professional officer corps, and equipment and training standards varied enormously from state to state because kit was raised locally rather than centrally. The Conscription Act of March 1863 substituted the draft and commutation for cash purchase, and black soldiers were permitted to enlist from 1862 onward, forming the United States Colored Troops. The navy grew from about one hundred and thirty vessels at the start of the war to more than six hundred by 1865, and in the process brought ironclads, contact mines and spar torpedoes into existence. The Confederacy was composed of eleven states, organised a government at Montgomery in February 1861 and moved it to Richmond in April. Its structural weakness lay in state sovereignty: each state decided for itself how many men to furnish, what to coin and whom to conscript, and a state governor could refuse a federal order. Military organisation and personnel stayed in state hands, which produced more than ten separately numbered state armies; even the Army of Northern Virginia and the Army of Tennessee under Lee and Johnston drew their recruits under state control. The Confederacy had no federal arsenal system, relied on state arsenals and on foreign purchase for its weapons, and its promotion pipeline broke down badly once the armies were massed.
people: 林肯是聯邦的樞紐。他在競選時以「一個國家不能一半奴隸一半自由」立論，當選後寧可承擔分裂的風險也不肯讓步；四月十八日的徵召令等於向南方攤牌，隨後他在葛底斯堡的演說中把這場戰爭重新定義為民族存亡之事。邦聯的戴維斯是西點出身的前美國陸軍部長，他在軍力與財政都到極限的情況下維持了政府的運作，但無法壓過州權。戰場上聯邦方面以格蘭特最見長，他自多納爾森與亨利堡取道維吉尼亞，此後經營維吉尼亞戰區，最後以消耗戰拿下彼得斯堡與里奇蒙；同時他具備政治手腕，能在議和與軍事之間周旋。羅伯特·李是邦聯最能打的指揮官，一八六二年六月接掌維吉尼亞軍，七月葛底斯堡挫敗之後再未取得決定性勝利。斯通瓦爾·傑克遜在謝南多厄河谷的奔襲與錢斯勒斯維爾的戰術是邦聯最傑出的軍事表現，可惜一八六三年陣亡。菲利普·謝里丹在謝南多厄河谷的焦土作戰與維吉尼亞後期的騎兵打擊，麥克萊倫在半島戰役與安提塔姆的保守用兵，李維斯與約翰斯頓早期的戰術安排，都是這場戰爭的樣本。約翰·巴福德與內森·貝德福德·福雷斯特代表邦聯騎兵，後者在北線以游擊破壞聯邦鐵路；聯邦方面的卡斯特在莫斯比圍剿中落敗後仍以冒進著稱。聯邦的財政靠財務卿蔡斯與華盛頓金融家傑伊·庫克主持，軍械供應靠科爾特的工廠以及斯賓塞、沙普、加特林等私人企業。廢奴派領袖弗雷德里克·道格拉斯親赴前線鼓動，並促成有色步兵團的成立；哈麗雅特·塔布曼在南卡羅來納的康巴希河區以夜間小隊襲擊，破解邦聯對黑人士兵的心理防線。南方方面，班納德·阿諾德由聯邦軍旅長轉投邦聯，被視為叛徒；約翰·莫西與約翰·摩根以游擊隊牽制北方兵力。
peopleEn: Lincoln was the hinge of the Union. He had campaigned on the proposition that a country could not be half slave and half free, and once elected he preferred to risk disunion rather than concede; his call for troops on 18 April amounted to putting the question to the South, and in his Gettysburg address he redefined the war as a test of national survival. Jefferson Davis, a West Point graduate and former United States secretary of war, kept the Confederate government running at the outer limit of its manpower and credit, but could not override the claims of the states. On the Union side Grant was the ablest of the commanders: he came up through Donelson and Henry, ran the Virginia theatre afterwards, and finished by taking Petersburg and Richmond through a war of attrition, and he had the political sense to move between negotiation and war. Robert Lee was the ablest Confederate commander, taking the Army of Northern Virginia in June 1862 and never winning a decisive engagement after Gettysburg in July. Stonewall Jackson's Shenandoah campaign and his performance at Chancellorsville were the finest Confederate operations of the war, and he was killed in 1863. Philip Sheridan's burning of the Shenandoah and his cavalry work in the closing Virginia campaigns, McClellan's cautious handling of the Peninsula and of Antietam, and the early tactical work of Lee and Johnston all belong to the same stock of examples. John Buford and Nathan Bedford Forrest stood for the Confederate cavalry, the latter harrying northern railroads by partisan war; Custer, after his failure in the Mosby country, remained noted for recklessness. The Union's finances were run by Secretary of the Treasury Chase and the Washington financier Jay Cooke, and its guns came from Colt's works and from private makers such as Spencer, Sharps and Gatling. Frederick Douglass went to the front to rally support and to press for the enrolment of black soldiers, and Harriet Tubman led night raids in the Combahee district of South Carolina, breaking the morale that the Confederacy hoped to maintain among the freedmen. On the southern side, Benedict Arnold passed from a Union brigade command to the Confederacy and was treated as a traitor, while John Mosby and John Morgan tied down northern strength with partisan bands.
kits: 卡面這件一八四〇年代法國雷管步槍的設計譜系，正是這場戰爭裡絕大部分步槍的母型。法國在一八四二年把密火點燃改為雷管底火，配用中空底槽的米涅球，射程與精度都遠超舊式火繩滑膛槍；英國一八五三年的恩菲爾德步槍與奧地利的洛倫茲一八四二年步槍都是它的近親，美國春田兵工場所造的斯普林菲爾德一八四二年式則是順著恩菲爾德再改的一代。戰爭中真正開火的是這些槍的量產版本：聯邦軍以斯普林菲爾德一八六一年式為主力，兵工場四年產出步槍逾一百四十萬支，另購入數十萬支英制恩菲爾德、三十萬支奧制洛倫茲與十餘萬支比利時「神秘」式步槍；邦聯靠北方的私人兵工廠仿製與密西西比本土仿造，加上倫敦與紐約商號的海外採購，前後取得十萬支左右仿製的斯普林菲爾德，另在本土造出數萬支粗糙的密西西比長槍。單發槍之外，交戰雙方都大量採購連發武器：科爾特公司在一八六三年供應聯邦約九萬支左輪手槍與二十萬支卡賓槍，斯賓塞連發卡賓槍約二萬五千支，Sharps 步槍與 Volcanic 連發槍數量較少但精準，另有十餘挺加特林機關槍少量試用。炮兵仍舊是拿破崙時代的樣子：聯邦大量使用帕羅特鑄鐵線膛炮與十二磅「拿破崙」野戰炮，邦聯以改裝舊炮與自行設計的布魯克線膛炮應對，後膛炮尚未普及。輔助裝備方面，聯軍以輜重車隊、輿車、救護車與隨軍浮橋配合作戰，馬匹大量損耗後難以補充，邦聯在馬匹與皮革上的短缺直接限制了其騎兵與砲列的續戰能力。
kitsEn: The design lineage of the French percussion rifle on this card is the parent of the overwhelming majority of the muskets used in this war. In 1842 France replaced the match with a percussion cap and adopted the hollow-base Minié ball, and both range and accuracy then outstripped the old matchlock smoothbore; the British Pattern 1853 Enfield and the Austrian Lorenz Model 1842 were both close relatives of it, and the Springfield Model 1842 made at the United States arsenal was in turn a further adaptation of the Enfield. What actually fired in this war were the mass-produced versions of those patterns. The Union leaned on the Springfield Model 1861, and the arsenal turned out more than one million four hundred thousand muskets in four years, while the government also bought several hundred thousand British Enfields, three hundred thousand Austrian Lorenzes and over a hundred thousand Belgian mystery rifles. The Confederacy obtained roughly a hundred thousand imitations of the Springfield made by private northern arsenals and in Mississippi, bought further weapons through London and New York houses, and built tens of thousands of crude long rifles of its own in Mississippi. Alongside the single-shot weapons both sides bought repeating arms heavily: Colt supplied the Union with roughly ninety thousand revolvers and two hundred thousand carbines in 1863, about twenty-five thousand Spencer repeating carbines were issued, Sharps rifles and Volcanic repeaters were fewer but accurate, and a handful of Gatling guns were tried out. The artillery was still Napoleonic in character: the Union used large numbers of cast-iron Parrott rifles and twelve-pounder field guns, the Confederacy answered with rebuilt old pieces and its own rifled Brooke gun, and breech-loading artillery was not yet in service. In the supporting train the Union marched with wagon trains, ambulances and pontoon bridges carried as part of the engineering equipment; horses wore out faster than they could be replaced, and the Confederate shortage of horses and leather directly limited the endurance of their cavalry and their batteries.
tactics: 雷管槍把有效射程推到二百至三百碼之後，拿破崙式的密集縱隊與齊射衝鋒在這一點上就走不下去。一八六二年十二月弗雷德里克斯堡，聯邦軍一天之內以一萬一千人渡過拉帕哈諾克河，縱隊沿泥濘灘地前進，被居高臨下的散兵與曲射炮火打成重創，一天陣亡與重傷逾一萬二千人；一八六四年六月冷港，格蘭特在不到一小時內以三次縱隊攻擊塹壕，傷亡近一萬八千人，此後再無人敢在未加掩護的正面強攻。與此同時，戰術重心從線式齊射轉向散兵線：南北兩軍普遍以連排展開、逐級進逼，森林地形與步槍射程使密集縱隊與散兵線的結合成為主流，縱隊不再整營前推，而以營為單位分批投入。炮兵的第一任務由支援射擊變成反炮兵戰，先以集中炮火壓制敵方炮位再讓步兵推進；圍城則依賴壕溝、胸口牆與地雷，彼得斯堡的地雷坑戰役中爆破提前引燃，四百磅炸藥炸開的坑洞反而成了進攻方的屠場。騎兵多不作正面衝鋒而作偵察、封鎖與襲擊後方，聯邦騎兵在戰爭末期獲得大量新式步槍與機關槍，卡斯特與謝里丹的快速縱隊擊敗南方殘存的騎兵。補給方面，維吉尼亞戰線的糧彈靠維吉尼亞鐵路與華盛頓至里奇蒙線輸送，缺點是南北向可用的鐵路僅得其一，一被破壞就靠數百輛馬車的縱隊接替，縱隊速度每天只走十至十二英里。戰略層面上，聯邦用封鎖與資源消耗壓死邦聯，一八六三年攻佔維克斯堡切斷密西西比河，邦聯失去半數兵力與西部出口；一八六四年謝爾曼自亞特蘭大向海進軍，把戰爭從會戰層面推到國民生產與運輸線的層面。
tacticsEn: Once the percussion rifle pushed effective range out to two hundred or three hundred yards, the Napoleonic close column and volley charge could no longer survive. In December 1862 at Fredericksburg eleven thousand Federal troops crossed the Rappahannock in a single day, marched in column over muddy ground, and were broken by plunging skirmish fire and curved artillery with more than twelve thousand casualties on the Union side. In June 1864 at Cold Harbor Grant launched three column attacks against the entrenchments in under an hour and lost nearly eighteen thousand men, and after that no one attempted a frontal assault without cover. At the same time the tactical centre of gravity moved from linear volley to skirmish line: both armies fought in extended order and advanced by bounds, and because of the woods and the reach of the musket the combination of close support and open order became normal, a whole battalion no longer advancing in line but fed forward in turn. The first task of the artillery changed from support to counter-battery, guns being massed against enemy batteries before the infantry was let forward; siege came to depend on trenches, breastworks and mines, and at the Crater outside Petersburg the mine was prematurely fired and the hole blown by some four hundred pounds of powder became a slaughter pen for the men who had set it. Cavalry was seldom used in frontal charge but for reconnaissance, screening and raiding behind the lines, and the Union horsemen late in the war were well armed with new rifles and repeaters, Custer's and Sheridan's fast columns beating the last Confederate cavalry. Supply in the Virginia theatre ran on the Virginia Central and the Orange and Alexandria lines, but the weakness was that only one usable north-south railway existed; once it was cut the trains were replaced by wagon columns of several hundred vehicles moving ten or twelve miles a day. At the strategic level the Union chose to crush the Confederacy by blockade and by exhaustion: the capture of Vicksburg in 1863 cut the Mississippi and removed half the Confederate army and the western outlet, and in 1864 Sherman's march from Atlanta to the sea lifted the war out of the battle line and into the country's production and transport.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下：戰爭自一八六一年四月十二日薩姆特堡開火，至一八六五年四月九日李維斯在阿波馬托克斯投降，前後約四年，全國被列為戰役與交火的事件以千計，其中被歸為大型會戰者約三百八十場。聯邦先後徵召入伍約三百五十萬人，其中正規陸軍約二百二十萬、海軍約九萬，另有各州民兵；邦聯合計約一百二十五萬至一百五十萬。戰爭結束時聯邦共三十五州，邦聯十一州全部回到聯邦。傷亡方面，聯邦陣亡與病亡合計約三十六萬，邦聯約二十五萬，其中直接戰鬥死亡分別約十六萬五千與九萬上下。會戰傷亡最重的幾場：葛底斯堡三日雙方合計約五萬一千人，安提塔姆一天雙方傷亡約二萬二千至二萬五千，弗雷德里克斯堡聯邦一軍傷亡一萬二千六百五十三人，冷港之戰聯邦傷亡近一萬八千，斯波特瑟爾維亞血角一役雙方合計約兩萬。一八六〇年美國鐵路總里程約三萬零六百英里，南方十一州合計不足九千英里，聯邦因此在鐵路供給上佔優。一八六四年聯邦兵工署的年報記錄步槍彈產量約一千二百七十萬發，南方各州同年合計不足五十萬發，南方步槍彈的儲備常以數日計；以每兵每日一發估算，維吉尼亞戰役前後四十日內聯邦軍的步槍彈消耗量超過三千五百萬發。戰費方面，聯邦政府直接支出約二十六億美元，加計各州支出與南方被毀的財產，全國總成本常被概估在二百億美元上下。一八六〇年美國人口約三千一百四十萬，其中被奴役者約三百五十萬至三百九十萬；一八六三年解放宣言生效時，聯邦軍在南方已接納逾五十萬名逃出莊園的被奴役者，黑人士兵入伍者約十八萬。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war opened with Fort Sumter on 12 April 1861 and ended with Lee's surrender at Appomattox on 9 April 1865, about four years in all; the engagements catalogued for the whole country run into the thousands, and about three hundred and eighty are classed as major battles. The Union enrolled about three and a half million men, of whom roughly two million two hundred thousand served in the regular army and ninety thousand in the navy, with state militia besides; the Confederacy accounted for somewhere between one million two hundred fifty thousand and one million five hundred thousand. At the end of the war the Union had thirty-five states and all eleven Confederate states had come back. On losses the Union dead, of battle and of disease, came to about three hundred sixty thousand and the Confederacy to about two hundred fifty thousand, of whom roughly one hundred sixty-five thousand and ninety thousand respectively were killed in battle. The heaviest single actions were Gettysburg, where about fifty-one thousand fell on both sides in three days; Antietam, with some twenty-two to twenty-five thousand casualties in a single day; Fredericksburg, where the Union army lost twelve thousand six hundred fifty-three men; Cold Harbor, where Union losses came close to eighteen thousand; and Spotsylvania's Bloody Angle, with about twenty thousand casualties on both sides. In 1860 American railways totalled some thirty thousand six hundred miles, of which the eleven Confederate states held fewer than nine thousand, and the Union therefore held the advantage in railborne supply. The federal ordnance department's report for 1864 records small-arms ammunition output of about twelve million seven hundred thousand rounds, while the Confederate states together produced under five hundred thousand in the same year, so that Confederate stocks of musket ammunition were commonly counted in days; estimating one round per man per day, the Union army burned more than thirty-five million rounds of small-arms ammunition in the forty days around the Virginia battles. In money the federal government spent about two and a half billion dollars directly, and once state expenditure and the destruction of southern property are added the total cost to the country is commonly put at around two billion dollars in the money of the day. The United States had about thirty-one million four hundred thousand people in 1860, of whom between three and a half and three million nine hundred thousand were enslaved; when the Emancipation Proclamation took effect in 1863 the Union army had already taken in more than half a million people who had left the plantations, and some one hundred eighty thousand black soldiers had enlisted.
cause: 起因是奴隸制與聯邦的國家形態無法共存。一八五〇年代廢奴派在政治上把自由土地與自由勞動綁在一起，一八五四年堪薩斯—內布拉斯加法廢除密蘇里妥協、允許兩地以全民投票決定奴隸制，隨即引發流血的堪薩斯，兩年之內該地驗證了投票造假、暴力掠奪與邊界衝突；一八五七年德雷德·斯科特判例更宣布黑人無權在聯邦土地取得公民權，廢奴問題於是由道德爭議變成憲制衝突。林肯與道格拉斯一八五八年的辯論把分歧講到無法迴避，同年哈雷特·比徹·斯托瓦爾的小說把廢奴者描寫為破壞社會的暴徒，一八五九年布朗突襲拉帕哈諾克河畔的武器庫，北方民主黨中的一部分選民因此倒向共和黨。一八六〇年大選，共和黨僅以不足四成的普選票贏得一百八十張選舉人票，南方各州在結果公布後視之為對奴隸制度存亡的威脅，南卡羅來納率先退出，隨後十州跟進。聯邦的廢奴派並未解散聯邦，林肯政府的選擇是把問題攤在桌上：一八六一年四月十八日的七萬五千人徵召令等於要求南方交出武裝，此令一經發出，維吉尼亞的聯邦軍退出，邦聯軍取而代之。里奇蒙兵工廠的軍械庫於四月三日被聯邦軍佔領，四月十二日邦聯炮兵向薩姆特堡開火，戰爭自此展開。
causeEn: The cause lay in the incompatibility between slavery and the form of the American state. In the 1850s the abolitionists tied free land to free labour in politics, and in 1854 the Kansas-Nebraska Act threw away the Missouri Compromise and allowed the two territories to decide on slavery by popular vote, which immediately produced Bleeding Kansas: within two years that territory had shown what voting fraud, forcible seizure and border war looked like, and the Dred Scott decision of 1857 went further and denied national citizenship to black people within the Union, turning an argument about morality into a constitutional one. The Lincoln-Douglas debates of 1858 drove the disagreement to the point of no evasion, and in the same year Harriet Beecher Stowe's novel pictured the abolitionist as a mobster, while Brown's raid on the arsenal at Harper's Ferry in 1859 pushed part of the northern Democratic vote towards the Republicans. In the election of 1860 the Republicans carried one hundred eighty electoral votes on less than forty per cent of the popular vote, and the southern states read the result as a threat to the survival of slavery: South Carolina left first and ten states followed. The abolitionists had not dissolved the Union, and the Lincoln administration chose to put the question in the open. The call for seventy-five thousand men on 18 April 1861 amounted to a demand that the South surrender its weapons, and the moment it went out the federal troops of Virginia left the state and Confederate troops took their place. The arsenal at Richmond was seized by federal forces on 3 April, and on 12 April Confederate artillery opened fire on Fort Sumter, and the war began.
impact: 影響是結構性的。軍事上，這場戰爭把步槍射程決定陣形的命題推到極致：此後任何參戰國在規劃野戰時都不能假設縱隊能抵近到一百碼，塹壕、散兵線與連發武器成為必備，德國、俄羅斯與日本的事後軍事學院大量翻譯美國戰例，歐洲的兵工制度亦被重新檢視。技術上，戰爭把槍枝、彈藥與零件變成一條可以規模生產的產業鏈：科爾特的左輪產量以數十萬計，春田兵工場的流水線與可互換零件成為工業動員的樣板，戰時建立的聯邦造幣、聯邦紙幣、一八六二年的所得稅與一八六三年的國民銀行法，開了以國家信用支撐大規模戰爭的先例。法律上，林肯在一八六三年四月二十四日頒布的第五十號軍令確立了戰時法紀，戰俘待遇、財產沒收與叛國行為的界線自此有明文可循，後來的公海公約與戰俘待遇規則都可在此找到源頭。國際上，聯邦用自由海權與反奴體制的說辯在歐洲取得道義位置，英國雖允許南方在利物浦建造私掠船，但最終未正式承認邦聯，一八七二年仲裁解決的阿拉巴馬索賠使英國付出七百七十萬美元，這套外交經驗此後成為美國界定正當戰爭的標準。國內轉變上，一八六三年一月一日的解放宣言使被奴役者獲得法律上的自由，約十八萬名黑人士兵編入聯邦軍，與一八六五年十二月在國會通過的第十三修正案共同把這場戰爭的戰果固定為制度性的廢奴。西部方面，一八六二年通過的宅地法與太平洋鐵路法把戰時的物資需求轉成對西部土地與鐵路的佔有，聯邦軍在西部對原住民的戰事與大平原的開發同步推進，戰爭的資源基礎正是這條鐵路；內布拉斯加與達科他准州的戰事、科羅拉多民兵在桑克里河流域的行動，以及戰後將五族強制遷出印地安領地的決定，使這場戰爭的戰果從南方延伸到西部，把聯邦國家的邊界與代價推到尚未被納入協議的地區。
impactEn: The consequences were structural. Militarily the war pushed to its extreme the proposition that the reach of the musket determines the formation: after it no belligerent could plan a field battle on the assumption that a column would close to a hundred yards, and entrenchments, skirmish lines and repeaters became mandatory; the staff colleges of Germany, Russia and Japan afterwards translated American cases in bulk, and European ordnance systems were re-examined. In technology the war turned gun, cartridge and part into a single chain of mass production: Colt turned out revolvers by the hundred thousand, the Springfield line and its interchangeable parts became the model of industrial mobilisation, and the federal mint, federal paper money, the income tax of 1862 and the National Banking Act of 1863 opened the precedent of financing a large war on national credit. In law, General Order No. 100, which Lincoln issued on 24 April 1863, fixed the rules of war, and the treatment of prisoners, confiscation and treason were thereafter bounded in writing; the later conventions on the high seas and on prisoners of war can be traced back to it. Internationally, the Union's appeal to the freedom of the seas and to the antislavery cause won it moral ground in Europe; Britain permitted the building of Confederate commerce raiders in Liverpool but never formally recognised the Confederacy, and the Alabama claims arbitrated in 1872 cost Britain seven million seven hundred thousand dollars. That diplomatic experience became the American standard for defining a just war. At home, the Emancipation Proclamation of 1 January 1863 made freedom a legal fact for the enslaved, and roughly one hundred eighty thousand black soldiers in the Union army, together with the Thirteenth Amendment passed by Congress in December 1865, fixed the outcome of the war as an institutional abolition. In the west, the Homestead Act and the Pacific Railway Act of 1862 turned the material demands of the war into possession of western land and western track; the Union's campaigns against the Indians advanced together with the settlement of the Great Plains, and the rail line was the resource base of the war itself. The fate of the native peoples changed as well: the fighting in Nebraska and Dakota, the action of the Colorado militia in the Sand Creek country, and the postwar decision to remove the Five Tribes from Indian Territory carried the war's consequences from the south into the west, pushing the limits and the costs of the Union state out into country that had never been party to the settlement.
result: 結果是聯邦的勝利，但勝利並非由任何一場會戰決定。一八六五年三月二十五日李維斯的軍隊退到阿波馬托克斯，格蘭特以近乎寬厚的條件接受投降，聯邦軍隨即向南方縱深推進，四月三日里奇蒙陷落，約翰斯頓在北卡羅來納的班尼特莊地投降；五月二日聯邦進入里奇蒙，總統乘火車抵達時，踏上的是自己祖宅所在的那條街。最後一支邦聯武裝是商船謝南多號，一八六五年十一月六日在利物浦投降，戰爭至此完全結束。帳面是這樣的：聯邦以約三百五十萬人對一百二十五萬人的兵力絕對優勢，靠鐵路、海軍封鎖與工業產能，把一場南方認為可以速戰速決的戰爭拖成四年的消耗；邦聯的敗因不在戰術而在結構——州權分散使兵力無法集中，工業基礎薄弱使彈藥槍械永遠短缺，外交上既未得到法國的正式承認，也未換來英國的干預。但勝利並未帶來自滿：林肯在葛底斯堡說這場戰爭的結果屬於我們，他的第二任期尚未開始即遭暗殺，一八六五年四月十四日他在福特劇院被南方支持者與邦聯舊軍人合謀刺殺，四月十五日去世，副總統安德魯·約翰遜繼任。戰後重建持續十年，聯邦以軍事佔領維持南方各州的廢奴與公民權，南方在憲法鬥爭中終以一八七七年的妥協收場，制度性成果大部分被削弱，但廢奴本身與聯邦的完整未被推翻。此後這場戰爭在美國記憶中分裂為兩條並行的敘事：一條是國家統一與自由的敘事，一條是失去的南方與被背叛的州的敘事，兩者在聯邦旗下的國旗、紀念碑與教科書裡拉鋸了一個多世紀。
resultEn: The result was a Union victory, but it was decided by no single engagement. On 25 March 1865 Lee's army withdrew to Appomattox and Grant accepted its surrender on terms of unusual leniency; the Federal armies then drove south, Richmond fell on 3 April, and Johnston surrendered at Bennett Place in North Carolina. The Union entered Richmond on 2 May, and the president arrived by train on a street that ran past his own boyhood house. The last Confederate force of arms was the commerce raider Shenandoah, which surrendered at Liverpool on 6 November 1865, and the war was then completely over. The ledger is this: the Union's three and a half million men against a hundred and twenty-five thousand more, a decisive advantage of numbers, applied through railways, naval blockade and industrial output, turned a war the South expected to be short into four years of exhaustion. The Confederacy's defeat lay not in tactics but in structure: dispersed state sovereignty prevented concentration of force, thin industrial capacity meant that ammunition and small arms were always short, and diplomatically it won neither formal recognition from France nor intervention from Britain. The victory brought no complacency. Lincoln said at Gettysburg that the outcome belonged to us, and his second term had not begun when he was shot: on 14 April 1865 he was assassinated at Ford's Theatre by a conspiracy of southern sympathisers and former Confederate soldiers, and died on 15 April, with Andrew Johnson succeeding him. Reconstruction ran for a decade, with military occupation sustaining abolition and the franchise in the southern states, and the South finally bought its way out of that settlement through the compromise of 1877, so that most of the institutional gains were undone, though emancipation itself and the integrity of the Union were not. Since then the war has split in American memory into two parallel narratives, one of national union and freedom and one of the lost South and the betrayed states, and the two have fought over flags, monuments and schoolbooks inside the same federal Union for more than a century.
